sample_unit: chest X-ray images (three public datasets: PadChest, NIH ChestX-ray14, MIMIC-CXR)

links.outcome: Accuracy-coverage trade-off when model abstains on uncertain chest X-ray predictions and defers to experts
links.effect: Selective rejection improved the trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and coverage; entropy-based rejection gave the highest average AuC across all pathologies. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Experiments conducted on three large public datasets (PadChest, NIH ChestX-ray14, and MIMIC-CXR) demonstrate that selective rejection improves the trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and coverage, with entropy-based rejection yielding the highest average AuC across all pathologies.

unlisted_practices: Entropy-based and confidence-interval-based selective prediction (rejection) with quantile-based threshold calibration, global or class-specific

screen.reason: Evaluates selective prediction / rejection mechanisms (entropy- and confidence interval-based abstention) as a safeguard to defer uncertain predictions to clinical experts in chest X-ray diagnosis.
